images.title: Mend the forgotten term
images.purpose: Shows −3p(−5p + 2q) wrongly simplified to p − 2q, struck out, and the correct 15p² − 6pq from multiplying both terms.
images.composition: A before and after comparison: the wrong answer struck out on the left, the mended working on the right. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: At the top centre, the label '−3p(−5p + 2q)'. Left: the label 'p − 2q' in grey (#6B7280) with a single straight strike line through it. Right: two arrows from the top expression, each to a teal (#0072B2) line: '(−3p)(−5p) = 15p²' and '(−3p)(2q) = −6pq'; below them the green (#009E73) answer label '15p² − 6pq'. Exactly 1 struck out answer, 2 arrows and 1 correct answer.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Check that every term inside the bracket was multiplied, with its sign.
images.description: Shows −3p(−5p + 2q) wrongly simplified to p − 2q, struck out, and the correct 15p² − 6pq from multiplying both terms.

image_decisions.why: Placing the wrong and mended versions side by side trains students to spot the skipped term.
